name: Niger
summary_text: Niger is dangerous for trans visitors — and newly criminalising: in March 2025 the junta's Charter of Refoundation explicitly outlawed “LGBTQIA+ practices or any other unnatural behavior” for the first time (Article 25). Junta rule, jihadist insurgency, no recourse.

sources.title: Niger | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): in March 2025 Niger explicitly outlawed consensual same-sex acts for the first time - Article 25 of the junta's Charter of Refoundation prohibits 'LGBTQIA+ practices or any other unnatural behavior' during the five-year transition. No specific penalties yet, but a 2023 draft penal code seeks up to 5 years for same-sex conduct, 20 years for conducting/witnessing a same-sex marriage ceremony, and 5 years for participating in or financing 'homosexual' organisations. Even before the charter, two women were prosecuted in 2023 under 'public indecency' provisions.

sources.title: Africa Live this week: 5-11 December 2022 - BBC News
sources.claim_summary: BBC News live coverage (Dec 2022): Niger lawmakers backed a motion to criminalise same-sex relationships - presented by MP Nana Djibou Harouna; came weeks after a Maradi court acquitted two women of lesbianism charges because no legislation existed.
AP News: Niger criminalised homosexuality under the junta's new penal code (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

sources.title: ‘Witch-hunt’ in Niger as military regime rounds up LGBTQ+ population | Global development | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (July 2026): 'Witch-hunt' in Niger as the military regime rounds up the LGBTQ+ population - at least 40 people arrested in a 'toxic' climate; fears of HIV/AIDS resurgence amid loss of access to PrEP drugs.

sources.title: Le Niger criminalise la Pratique LGBTQIA+ dans le pays - Agence Nigérienne de Presse
sources.claim_summary: Agence Nigérienne de Presse (in French): 'Le Niger criminalise la pratique LGBTQIA+ dans le pays' - official Nigerien press coverage of the criminalisation (page largely navigation content at fetch time).
